items.title: 007 First Light Is Getting Free DLC Later This Week
items.excerpt: 007 First Light is getting new, free DLC later this week.
items.content_text: 007 First Light is getting new, free DLC later this week. IO Interactive has teased the new DLC via a short video on its socials, confirming it will arrive on Thursday, October 2. The DLC will be free, but as of right now, IO is remaining tight-lipped about what it will include. However, based on some prior info, we can likely assume that this is the long-awaited Aston Martin Valhalla update. This content has been teased since launch in the game's main menu, and it appears it's finally being added to the game. This is expected to include a new TacSim mission featuring the Aston Martin Valhalla, which is used near the end of the game as part of a massive set piece. Given the extensive wait, it seems hard to imagine this will be just a short, single TacSim mission. This may add some other items that were revealed as part of a larger roadmap for the game , such as new game+, new gadgets, and other missions and content. A free DLC is just around the bend. Tune in on October 1st. #007FirstLight #EarnTheNumber pic.twitter.com/9uCpNDTPth — 007 First Light (@007GameIOI) September 29, 2026 We'll just have to sit tight and wait to see what exactly is in store, though. 007 First Light is also set to get a new story DLC centered around Bawama, the pirate king warlord played by Lenny Kravitz. There's no firm release date for that content, though it's expected to be a premium add-on rather than a free update like what's coming later this week. 007 First Light's Nintendo Switch 2 port is also still coming down the pipeline. It was expected to be out by now, but was recently pushed to 2027 to ensure it was as good as it could be for fans. It's unclear for how long IO Interactive plans to support this game, as it has continued to drop updates for Hitman many years after its release. Even without a steady stream of post-launch content, 007 First Light has been a big hit. The game sold 4 million copies in its first three months , and sequels are expected to follow, though it will likely be a while before they materialize.
items.title_en: 007 First Light Is Getting Free DLC Later This Week

items.title: Jennifer Lawrence to Star in Zach Cregger’s Sci-Fi Thriller The Flood
items.excerpt: Zach Cregger’s next movie, a science fiction thriller called The Flood, is set to release in theaters on August 11, 2028.
items.content_text: Zach Cregger’s next movie, a science fiction thriller called The Flood , is set to release in theaters on August 11, 2028. Cregger is writing, producing, and directing the film, which will star Jennifer Lawrence, as confirmed by Variety on September 29, 2026. Warner Bros. and New Line Cinema are slated to distribute the movie, which is being produced by Amblin Entertainment and Vertigo Entertainment's Roy Lee and Miri Yoon. Thus far, other cast members and specific plot details have been kept secret, but Cregger has given us a few insights into what we can expect from his forthcoming sci-fi flick. Speaking to Men’s Health in mid-September, Cregger revealed that the movie is 'similar' to Stanley Kubrick’s 2001: A Space Odyssey . “I'm not comparing [The Flood] to 2001, because I think 2001 is a true masterpiece in every sense of the word. But there's a bizarreness to that movie that's really undeniable, and it's also a horror movie. I think 2001 is a really thrilling horror movie about human nature, and obviously about artificial intelligence, but it asks big questions. And I think, in that way, there's some similarity with Flood,” he said. Based on these remarks, we can safely assume that The Flood has something to do with AI, human nature, and big-picture concepts — but one thing he confirmed was that The Flood is very specifically not a horror movie. “It unfolds in a very unique way that I'm really proud of. It's disturbing, but it's not a horror movie, although there are horror scenes in it. It feels intimidating to me. I'm still not really sure how to make it, but I think that's a good thing,” he clarified. “It's hard to talk about it without talking about the story. I’m thrilled to have the opportunity to make that movie. I’m in love with that story in a really unique way." This news comes hot on the heels of Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation, which released to overwhelmingly positive reviews among both fans of the games and film critics alike. It became the single most-successful Resident Evil movie ever, and even helped boost sales for Resident Evil 2 Remake by 50% on PlayStation 5. Cregger is best known for horror flicks like Barbarian and Weapons , so it’ll be interesting to see his take on a science fiction thriller. He isn’t the only big director in the horror space with exciting news to share, either, as Obsession director Curry Barker’s next movie, a horror-comedy titled Anything But Ghosts, has received a theatrical release date for May 7, 2027. items.title: Obsession Director Curry Barker's Next Film, Anything But Ghosts, Gets May 2027 Theatrical Release
items.excerpt: Obsession director Curry Barker’s next film, Anything But Ghosts, is coming to theaters next year.
items.content_text: Obsession director Curry Barker’s next film, Anything But Ghosts, is coming to theaters next year. Anything But Ghosts comes to the silver screen on May 7, 2027. The film takes place in the same universe as Obsession , but is classified as a horror-comedy that follows a different cast of characters entirely — though they also go through some seriously spooky stuff. Barker’s next flick stars Bryce Dallas Howard, Aaron Paul, Violet McGraw, Chris Reinache, and Cooper Tomlinson, who notably played Bear’s best friend, Ian, in Obsession, as well as Barker himself. Anything But Ghosts centers around two fake paranormal investigators who are finally confronted with some actual, real-life ghosts (or would that be ‘real-afterlife’ ghosts?), causing things to “spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control,” as per an official press release. Speaking on a June episode of Raiders of the Lost Podcast , Tomlinson confirmed that he and Curry are playing the two phony ghost hunters, and described the film as “if Key and Peele walked into Hereditary.” “It’s a buddy comedy, you know, about these two guys, and it turns really scary,” he said. “You know, it’s about these con artist ghost hunters who encounter real ghosts, and then they have to step up and be the thing that they promised this family.” Both Barker and Tomlinson are producing and co-writing the film, which is produced by Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Focus holds the movie’s worldwide rights, and Universal Pictures International is handling international distribution for the studio. This is the second time Focus and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have worked together on a Curry Barker film; the two production houses also collaborated on Obsession, which released to rave reviews earlier this year. Barker’s next offering has a lot to live up to; Obsession became one of the world's most profitable films compared to its budget in history, receiving critical acclaim and becoming an instant horror classic. Inde Navarrette’s standout performance as Nikki catapulted her to international fame, helping her land the role of Rogue in Marvel’s X-Men reboot , and put Barker in the hotseat for studios looking to get in on his future projects. If you’ve ever watched Barker and Tomlinson’s humorous YouTube videos , you can safely assume that their delightful chemistry will get ample time to shine in Anything But Ghosts. With hard-hitters like Breaking Bad’s Aaron Paul and Jurassic World’s Bryce Dallas Howard in the mix, there’s no telling what hijinks these two will get up to, but we can almost guarantee it’ll be hilarious. And given how creepy Obsession managed to be on such a small budget, it feels like the Hereditary -ness of it all might also give us a few good scares, too. Image Credits: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images for IMDb

items.title: Coinbase Joins Pokémon TCG Hype With Its Own Digital Pack-Opening Service
items.excerpt: Coinbase is joining the Pokémon TCG craze with its own digital pack-opening platform.
items.content_text: Coinbase is joining the Pokémon TCG craze with its own digital pack-opening platform. Coinbase, a US-based cryptocurrency exchange platform, is moving in on the TCG market with a particular focus on Pokémon. At least, that’s what it seems like, based on a tweet it published on September 28. “Your binder is about to get a major upgrade,” the post reads. “Rip packs on your phone. Every pull backed by a real, physical card. Vault it or ship it. Soon on Coinbase.” Your binder is about to get a major upgrade. Rip packs on your phone. Every pull backed by a real, physical card. Vault it or ship it. Soon on Coinbase. pic.twitter.com/Utfwq30DSj — Coinbase 🛡️ (@coinbase) September 28, 2026 While the post’s text doesn’t mention Pokémon by name, the accompanying image attached to it shows mockups of five Pokémon TCG card packs that are labeled ‘Pokémon’ with the numbers 1-5. The platform also responded to a few comments that mentioned the popular monster-catching franchise; one user wrote, “Pokémon packs on the chain, trading cards just hit peak convenience,” to which it replied, “You get it.” “STFU, Coinbase is going to partner with and onboard everything on earth,” another wrote, to which Coinbase responded, “Well, we are the Everything Exchange.” Based on this post, it looks like Coinbase users will soon be able to open digital card packs, with the option to place those cards in a digital ‘vault’ or receive their physical equivalent by mail. However, another reply from Coinbase suggests there’ll be some additional features at play; one user wrote, “The vaulting aspect is the real game changer here,” to which it replied, “And there’s more…” For now, details remain sparse. We don’t know how Coinbase’s status as a crypto platform will impact its attempt at a pack-opening service, nor how it intends to grade said cards or provide proof of ownership. Will these pulls come from pre-opened packs? Who’s to say. It’s also worth noting that such a service, sans cryptocurrency, already exists; as pointed out by Dexerto , Gamestop’s Power Packs program also features a digital option, allowing customers to open mystery packs online and receive those cards’ physical counterparts. Gamestop assures its buyers that every digital pack contains a "real, authenticated item” that they can either hold in their digital PSA vault, have shipped to them, or take advantage of its instant buyback program and use those funds to purchase another card pack. It remains to be seen if Coinbase will provide similar guarantees. Coinbase’s proposed pack-opening platform comes on the heels of Pokémon’s 30th Anniversary celebration, which has shone a spotlight on the ever-growing hype around the card collecting scene, as well as the scalpers who have caused chaos during its special merchandise and card launches. For instance, the special 30th Anniversary card pack drops at retailers like Target and other shops prompted long lines outside stores as mobs of fans showed up for the chance at snagging some packs for themselves, with some even ‘reserving’ spots in line by setting out chairs with no one sitting in them.

items.title: Pokémon VGC Pro Begs Players to Wash Themselves After Opponent’s 'Putrid' Stench Makes Them Vomit
items.excerpt: A professional Pokémon player is going viral after begging his fellow competitors to keep up with their personal hygiene, claiming he literally threw up at an event due to someone’s stench.
items.content_text: A professional Pokémon player is going viral after begging his fellow competitors to keep up with their personal hygiene, claiming he literally threw up at an event due to someone’s stench. Texas-based Pokémon VGC regional champion Donghun Youm says he lost his lunch at the 2026 Baltimore Regional Championships thanks to a super smelly player. Youm wrote about his experience in a viral post on Twitter/X, where he begged players to “please take care of [their] personal hygiene.” Youm said someone at the competition smelled so foul that he literally threw up because of it, and his friends were unable to concentrate on their own matches due to the putrid stench. “I've had an incident at Baltimore regionals where I had to throw up due to a nearby player's stench,” he said. “My friends and I couldn't focus that round due to how putrid the smell was, and we even told a judge due to it. Like, c'mon man....” Youm’s post has kicked off a heated discourse about players’ hygiene at competitions, as well as no end of jokes and memes about certain Pokémon attacks that rely on smell to deal damage or inflict adverse status effects. (The ability ‘Stench’ was most popular, as it has a 10% chance of making your opponent flinch when hit by a damaging move.) Please take care of your personal hygiene. I've had an incident @ Baltimore regionals where I had to throw up due to a nearby player's stench. My friends and I couldn't focus that round due to how putrid the smell was and we even told a judge due to it. Like c'mon man.... — Donghun Youm (@PlaymakerYoum) September 27, 2026 “[Washing] should be a requirement to attend an event,” one commenter replied. “People who smell bad should be kicked out.” “If you can afford a Nintendo Switch, you can afford a $3 stick of deodorant dude,” another said. This is far from the first time the subject of hygiene has come up regarding in-person gaming events; in June, a card shop in Oregon suspended its Yu-Gi-Oh tournaments after receiving bad reviews and multiple complaints of smelly patrons. The shop pointed to Konami’s own tournament guidelines, which stipulate that everyone at a Yu-Gi-Oh competition, not just players, must be “clean and wear clean clothing,” or risk being “penalized.” Pokémon boasts similar rules; the official Play! Pokemon Tournament Rules Handbook includes a section regarding hygiene, which reads, “Individuals are also required to maintain a socially acceptable level of hygiene during the event. Depending on the attire or level of hygiene, the Tournament Organizer may allow for a tournament participant to change or update their personal hygiene and attire and return to the venue. "If a participant refuses to comply with tournament staff’s requests, this is grounds for removal from the tournament and venue, and the participant must relinquish their badge to tournament staff." It’s unclear if the stinky player who caused Youm to throw up was penalized. Either way, the incident has sparked renewed calls from community members for their fellow players to keep themselves clean and fresh at competitions to avoid unpleasant situations like this one.

items.title: Everything Coming to Apple TV in October
items.content_text: Unlike streaming services like Peacock and Disney+ , Apple TV isn’t really leaning into the Halloween vibes this year. Instead, the streaming platform is opting to stay the usual course of prestige original shows, movies, and documentaries. It is, however, still home to the Peanuts holiday specials, and even if you aren’t a subscriber, you’ll be able to watch "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" for free the weekend of Saturday, October 17. If you are subscribed to Apple TV, however, here’s what else you have to look forward to next month. New Series and Movies Coming to Apple TV in October The Last First: Winter K2 - October 2 Apple TV is getting one new documentary in October, which happens to be one of two new additions about climbing. Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, The Last First: Winter K2 was filmed back in 2021, when a group of climbers tried to ascend the titular second-highest mountain on Earth. The documentary will be coming to Apple TV after its premiere at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. The Sisters Grimm Season 2 - Premieres October 2 One of the only family-friendly additions of the month, The Sisters Grimm is premiering its second season on October 2. The animated series, which is based on Michael Buckley’s graphic novels, follows two relatively modern sisters who discover a town full of fairy tales. Small Prophets - October 7 Apple TV might be known for its thrillers and sci-fi, but it’s also home to some genre-bending comedies like Widow’s Bay. Hoping to join the better ranks of that list is Small Prophets, a six-part series that follows an aging man who turns to alchemy and magical spirits to find his one true love. Despite premiering on BBC Two earlier this year, unfortunately this one won’t be available to UK subscribers until 2027. Matchbox the Movie - October 9 A series of projects based on various Mattel toys got the green light after the success of Greta Gerwig’s Barbie . One of those projects is now coming to fruition as Matchbox the Movie, inspired by the titular toy car line. John Cena stars as Sean, an undercover CIA agent who enlists his childhood friend group to help save the world. Where’s Wanda? Season 2 - Premieres October 21 The darkly funny German series Where’s Wanda is returning for a second season toward the end of the month. While Carlotta and Deda managed to get some semblance of their lives back in Season 1, yet another crisis with their daughter, Wanda, threatens to tear their family apart again. New episodes every Wednesday. Tenzing - October 16 Tenzing is based on the true story of Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary, the first climbers to summit Mount Everest. Genden Phuntsok and Tom Hiddleston as the legendary climbers, who have their worldviews challenged by both the harrowing climb and each other. The film will receive a limited theatrical release starting October 9 before its Apple TV streaming premiere on October 16. Nocturne - October 30 An entirely new Apple Original series, Nocturne is loosely based on the Joona Linna crime novels by Lars Kepler, the pen name for Alexander Ahndoril and Alexandra Coelho Ahndoril. It stars Liev Schreiber as Jonah Lynn, a detective who heads to a small Pennsylvania town embroiled in the threat of a serial killer’s return. New episodes every Friday. Full Apple TV Schedule for October 2026 October 2 The Last First: Winter K2 The Sisters Grimm Season 2 (Premiere) Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 6 - “What the Universe is Made of” October 7 Small Prophets (All Episodes Streaming) Last Seen: Season 1, Episode 6 (Final) Ted Lasso: Season 4, Episode 10 (Final) Brothers: Episode 4 - "The Band" Slow Horses: Season 6, Episode 4 - “Lost and Found” October 9 Matchbox the Movie Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 7 - “The Pyramid” October 14 Brothers: Episode 5 - "Valentine's Day" Slow Horses: Season 6, Episode 5 - “Sayonara” October 16 Tenzing Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 8 - “The Basic Oneness of Everything” October 17 "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" (Streaming for Free) October 18 "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" (Streaming for Free) October 21 Brothers: Episode 6 - "The Dance" Slow Horses: Season 6 - “Judgement Day” (Final) October 23 Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 9 - “How to Build the Box” October 28 Brothers: Episode 7 - "The Interview" October 30 Nocturne (Premiere) Dark Matter: Season 2, Episode 10 - “No Quiet Life” Apple TV Plans and Prices Apple TV continues to offer one ad-free subscription plan at $14.99/month, though that plan is now included in iCloud+ memberships . The service also recently launched its first official bundle with Peacock , which knocks about 30% off the standard price of having both subscriptions. If you’re just looking for a taster (or a specific binge-watch), Apple TV is one of the only remaining streaming services to offer a full seven-day free trial . Extended free trials are also included in most Apple purchases, including the new line of iPhones .

items.title: Halo's Former Franchise Creative Director Sees 3 Possible Paths for Activision's Halo
items.excerpt: Frank O'Connor, Halo's Franchise Creative Director for nearly 20 years at 343 Industries/Halo Studios, has weighed in on Halo's future at Activision, suggesting three viable paths forward for Xbox's former biggest franchise.
items.content_text: Frank O'Connor, Halo's Franchise Creative Director for nearly 20 years at 343 Industries/Halo Studios (who, fun fact, was once my colleague at Official Xbox Magazine), has weighed in on Halo's future at Activision , suggesting three viable paths forward for Xbox's former biggest franchise. O'Connor, who moved on from 343 Industries in 2023, was responding to a post on LinkedIn by former Xbox Social Media Manager of Executive Communications Genevieve Harrison about Halo's move to Activision. Harrison was discussing how Activision might approach Halo, and said in part, "Talent is not a SharePoint folder you drag from /Call of Duty into /Halo and wait for the little green checkmark. What Activision does know how to do is run the absolute hell out of a giant franchise. Maybe that operational discipline is exactly what Halo needs. But Activision isn’t riding in to save Xbox either. Microsoft paid $68.7 billion for Activision Blizzard. Activision is Xbox. Maybe it works. I hope it does because I’d love another great Halo game." O'Connor, who started on the Halo franchise when he left Official Xbox Magazine to join Bungie during Halo 2's development, replied with his thoughts on how the series's next step at its new developer and publisher might go. "There are 3 paths - any one of which COULD be successful," he said. "None of these are easy, guaranteed or necessarily viable: 1. Make a "classic" Halo movement/sandbox/shooter experience tailored to a core audience & scaled to be successful with that core audience and attractive to a broader one so it can grow (not to mention obvious fact that Halo MP is better w. more people playing, by mathematical default). "2. Make something new, modern that >reinvents< the game/universe in a surprising but fantastic way. An action/sandbox game (maybe it's a new take on the FPS, maybe it's an action RPG but it's fundamentally different) and succeeds with a combination of strong story, IP use and gets a small head start based on curiosity or loyalty. "3. Translate Halo IP and sandbox into the ATVI comfort zone. Use the player, progression and business models that are proven to work and craft a big annual or semi-annual spectacle and constant content. Pro-Tip: Do NOT tie it to hardware/services launch cycles, do not try to force it into a shape (or aging platform) that it can't fit and do NOT abandon sandbox. Pro-Pro-Tip: Hire Bungie, Halo Studios and other laid off folk who are bursting w. talent and ideas that got nerfed or shut down over the years." Halo Studios went through a rebranding effort (from 343 Industries), a leadership shakeup, and a pivot to Unreal Engine as its underlying game technology in 2024, and shipped the multiplayer-less remake of the original Halo, called Halo: Campaign Evolved, earlier this year. However, the studio was reportedly years away on its next mainline Halo project ahead of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and Xbox COO Matt Booty's decision to hand Halo to the House of Call of Duty. I've since written about whether or not Activision can save Halo , but I'm not as convinced on the creative side, while my colleague Matt Purslow wrote about how, no matter what, Halo must go beyond Bungie's original template .
items.title_en: Halo's Former Franchise Creative Director Sees 3 Possible Paths for Activision's Halo

items.title: Game of Thrones Movie Aegon’s Conquest Sets 2029 Release Date With Director Owen Harris
items.excerpt: Warner Bros. has officially set a June 1, 2029 release date for Game of Thrones: Aegon's Conquest, with Owen Harris attached to direct.
items.content_text: Warner Bros. has officially announced a release date and director for Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest , the first feature film to stem from the HBO franchise. Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest will open in theaters on June 9, 2029. Owen Harris will direct from a screenplay by Beau Willimon (House of Cards). The film will adapt material from George R.R. Martin’s Targaryen history book, Fire & Blood. Harris is no stranger to Game of Thrones, having directed episodes of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms . Harris also directed three acclaimed episodes of Black Mirror ("Be Right Back", "San Junipero", and "Striking Vipers"). Martin’s Fire & Blood chronicles the history of the dragon-riding Targaryen dynasty, including the Dance of the Dragons civil war depicted in House of the Dragon . The Targaryens arrived in Westeros following the Doom of Valyria , settling on the island of Dragonstone . By the time Aegon reached adulthood, he made it his mission to unite the long-warring Seven Kingdoms under the rule of one man: himself. Aegon I Targaryen is responsible for countless deaths in his quest to become the sole ruler of the realm. He’s aided by his sister-wives Visenya and Rhaenys. All three siblings fly fearsome dragons: Aegon rides Balerion the Black Dread , Visenya rides Vhagar (yes, the same giant beast flown by Aemond in House of the Dragon ), and Rhaenys flies Meraxes. Aegon battles a slew of kingdoms during the Conquest, but his two biggest adversaries are King Harren the Black, the wicked lord of Harrenhal , and Meria Martell, the princess of Dorne. Meria and Dorne’s resistance against Aegon the Conqueror was notably recalled by Ormund Hightower to Daeron Targaryen in House of the Dragon Season 3, Episode 5. The Game of Thrones series has established that Aegon knew about the White Walkers and passed this secret knowledge down the generations from ruler to ruler. Aegon foresaw a great looming terror in the North, which convinced him that a Targaryen must occupy the Iron Throne when that dark day arrives to ensure humanity’s survival. Bringing Aegon’s Conquest to the big screen poses a host of challenges for the filmmakers, several of which I break down here .

items.title: 50-Minute AI-Generated Doctor Who Episode Is 'Pretty Good,' BBC Boss Says
items.excerpt: The BBC's new director general has described an AI-generated Doctor Who episode as "pretty good," and suggested that the technology enabled the creation of content "at the standard of a Hollywood studio."
items.content_text: The BBC's new director general has described a 50-minute AI-generated episode of Doctor Who as "pretty good," and suggested that the technology now enabled the creation of content "at the standard of a Hollywood studio." Brittin became boss of the UK's iconic broadcasting company in May this year, after almost two decades at Google, where he wound up working as the company's UK managing director. Now in charge of the BBC, Brittin faces a tough task of making further drastic cuts to the corporation's spending, while it continues to try and produce world-class programming — including its flagship sci-fi adventure series that's currently on hiatus after a disastrous few years. Doctor Who fans largely agree that their favorite show has declined in quality over the years, but especially over the past two seasons which featured Ncuti Gatwa in the role, and the return of Russell T Davies as showrunner. After just two seasons, this era of the show was unceremoniously ended when co-funding partner Disney ditched the series, prompting the departure of Gatwa in a reshot ending. A later promise to mount a one-off Christmas special that could tie-up the era's remaining plotlines was later scrapped too, with Davies and production company Bad Wolf also exiting. Now, the BBC has begun looking for a fresh production house to take the show on — a process it wants to result in new episodes of the series arriving in either 2028 or 2029. "Somebody sent me a 50-minute episode of Doctor Who that was AI-generated the other day," Brittin said, speaking at the Royal Television Society conference in London this week (thanks, Variety ). "It's pretty good. I mean, it's not going to replace humans, and we'll come on to that "So everyone's a creator. Not all the creativity is bad," Brittin continued. "Everyone's got the ability in their hands — or six billion people have — to create content at the standard of a Hollywood studio." While Brittin does not name the AI project he watched, it is almost certainly the 50-minute first episode of fan-made project The Unmade Season , which features a AI-made continuation of the series. Having watched a chunk of this myself, I'd say it is as good as you'd expect AI to be — which is to say, almost photorealistic but narratively still pretty flawed. The show picks up with a new incarnation of the Doctor who regenerates from David Tennant's 14th Doctor, played a Scottish-sounding AI actor. Scenes feature various AI oddities, though also incorporate various familiar Doctor Who monsters, such as Slitheen and Ood. All in all, it's not very good. And as a Doctor Who fan, it is particularly odd to hear the boss of the BBC offering any sort of praise to content, even non-commercial fan content, that appears to have been generated by regurgitating the BBC's own copyrighted episodes. While budgets may be tight, here's hoping this is the extent of the BBC's relationship to AI with Doctor Who going forward.
items.title_en: 50-Minute AI-Generated Doctor Who Episode Is 'Pretty Good,' BBC Boss Says

items.title: GTA 6: All the Major New Details Revealed Today, Including Animal Species, Side Activities, and Fast Travel
items.excerpt: We've rounded up all of the major GTA 6 details revealed in the latest Game Informer cover story.
items.content_text: Game Informer's GTA 6 coverage reveal has shed new light on Rockstar's upcoming game, and we've rounded up all the big new information. In the story, Rockstar shared new details about GTA 6's ambitious weather systems , the wildlife and NPCs that populate the world, and the scope of GTA 6's map. Hurricanes in GTA 6 Are Confirmed Rockstar has managed to pull off one of the most speculated parts of GTA 6: hurricanes. Fans were hoping to see Florida's most significant weather event replicated in GTA 6, but given how intense hurricanes are, many wondered if it was even technically feasible. Speaking to Game Informer, Rockstar confirmed they will be featured in the game, but declined to share how often they will happen and if they will impact the story. As for how they will be depicted, fans can expect “heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics, and a lot of rain combine so that everything is dripping wet, water is gushing off roof edges and lampposts, thunder rumbles and flashes of lightning light up the clouds dramatically.” Rockstar Re-Engineered Its Weather System for GTA 6; Will Feature Realistic Rainbows Rockstar's VP of art for lighting and rendering, Owen Shepherd, confirmed that the studio re-engineered its weather system to allow for localized, persistent, and dynamic weather. The player can soak up sunny rays in one part of the map, but still be able to see a rainstorm in the distance. The game will also feature rainbows and puddles, allowing the player to travel through an area and deduce that it recently rained there without having been present for it. Additionally, wind will create ripples in the water, blow hair around, and push debris across the world. Rockstar's Biggest, Most Dense Map to Date Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut confirmed that GTA 6's map is twice as big as GTA 5's, with an emphasis on density. The setting of the game, as many know, is a fictionalized version of Florida known as Leonida. "This new world is different," Garbut said. "We obsessed about every part – the rooftops, the alleys, the internals and everything in between to the point we hit a critical mass with the numbers of our interiors, and you start to feel the buildings are more real inside and out. This world is a cohesive whole with the density of content and a hand-crafted quality to every bit." GTA 6's Map Has Six Unique Regions GTA 6's map will feature six different regions. The most prominent one is Vice City, a location fans are familiar with thanks to 2002's GTA: Vice City. The other regions of Leonida include Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park. GTA 6's Regions May Have Different Factions to Contend With Ambrosia is a more rural part of the map with factories and refineries, dominated by a biker gang who control the area. This gang appears to be different from the Lost MC, which were prominently featured in GTA 4 and GTA 5. GTA 6's Story Is Designed to Take Players Across the Map With a map as big as Rockstar is promising, GTA 6 may feel daunting to would-be explorers. However, Rockstar plans to use the game's story to take players around the map and show off the different areas. Of course, this won't cover every inch of the world, but it will demonstrate the strong contrast of more affluent parts of Leonida versus more "poor" areas. GTA 6 Will Have a Fast Travel System GTA has historically let players hop in a cab to freely fast travel through the world, but Red Dead Redemption 2 was a bit more restrictive. You could fast travel from town to town, but not any hyper specific points on the map. GTA 6 will allow you to hop in a ride share car and zip around town... however, ride sharing means just that: sharing. Players will be able to share rides with other passengers and have unique conversations. You Can Doomscroll in GTA 6 If you don't want to make conversation with other passengers or sightsee, you can doomscroll on Snapmatic, the game's parody of Instagram. You Can't Post on Social Media Yourself, Though Players won't be able to post on the app themselves, as Jason and Lucia are on the run and would risk danger by being overly active on social media. Some of GTA 6's Side Activities Revealed GTA 6 will feature a boatload of side activities; here are just some of them, as revealed in Game Informer's story: • Base Jumping • Billiards • Gyms • Kayaking • Mini Golf • Scuba Diving • Street & Off-Road Racing • Zoos • Air Boating • Jet Skiing GTA 6 Has Over 170 Animal Species Fans will be able to see and interact with 170 different types of animals. This includes over 60 birds, over 30 land mammals, and a variety of fish and reptiles. The extended gameplay reveal in August confirmed that players will be able to pet dogs and if it's anything like Red Dead Redemption 2, this will presumably extend to other animals like cats. “Florida has a diverse animal ecosystem that we wanted to faithfully include across the different biomes in Leonida – urban and rural environs, aquatic life both inland and ocean, and the wetland habitats like the swamps and Everglades,” Rockstar vice president of dynamic art, Michael Kane, explained. “The animal art and population teams are incredibly passionate about delivering animals that are accurately researched and look visually correct in every respect, alongside the supporting movement and animation to bring them to life.” Aquatic Animals Will Have Distinct Behavior Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 features different shark species, jellyfish, whales, turtles, and rays in the game's sea. They will have "distinct movement behavior" and can be encountered while scuba diving in the water. Hunting Seemingly Returns One of the screenshots in Game Informer's story shows Jason approaching deer in the wild with a rifle strung over his back. It seems to suggest some form of hunting will return in the game. Hunting was a very small part of GTA 5 and a bit half-baked. The system returned in Red Dead Redemption 2 with significantly more depth. Animal Tracking and Rare Animals Return Players will be able to track animals as they did in Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar also confirmed there will be rare animal types, but didn't reveal any. Multiple Ways to Rob Robberies are a central part of the game and players will have a lot of choice in how they do that. Do they go as a duo? Do they go alone? Do they go loud? Do they go quiet? There are a lot of options, but your choices will determine the level of response you can get from the police. Busted Jason and Lucia can shake the cops together or split up, leaving one person to take the bulk of the heat. However, if either one of these protagonists gets overwhelmed by police, it's game over. Carjacking Has More Variety and Risks in GTA 6 Higher end cars require special tools to steal and if successful, they may have trackers or security systems to create new obstacles for you. Players can use an app known as WAiNK to determine a car's resale value, security system, and the cost to make it your own personal vehicle. Should you want to off-load it, you'll have to take it to a fence. Jason and Lucia's Relationship Is Influenced by Player Choice The two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, may long for a romantic relationship together, but it is up to the player to determine whether or not they go beyond a platonic one. The player will be able to essentially court the two characters by taking them on dates, paying attention when they call or text you, and being chivalrous by opening doors or holding hands. Choices Shape GTA 6's Story GTA 6's story will be ripe for multiple playthoughs. Rockstar confirmed that choices big and small with not only influence Jason and Lucia's relationship, but the story as a whole, encouraging players to play the game again to see alternative story threads. Rockstar Is Trying to Overdeliver on Players' Sky High Expectations “As the pressure for us on this project is huge, we dealt with that by doing our best to overdeliver," said Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut. "Normally you compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction, but with this project we went the other way - everything is dialed up – detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction and density. I don't think we have ever created anything close to this before." GTA 6 Will Feature an Absurdly Diverse Set of NPCs Rockstar has created a wide variety of NPCs that vary in height, weight, skin type, and more. Characters can get a tan, they can have moles, and even the sizes of their butts and chests will vary from person to person. GTA 6 Features the Biggest Collection of Clothing and Accessories to Date GTA 6 will feature a ton of clothing options, which players can acquire with their ill-gotten gains. NPCs will also be dressed differently based on where they are in the world. If they're in a more impoverished area, expect them to have dirtier or weathered clothing. “We’ve been able to really go hard on that with creating the biggest range of garments and accessories we’ve ever made – supported with rich, realistic materials,” Kane says. “That surfacing includes color, patterns and branding that are both area-appropriate, but also tied to context (states of dirt/weathering and fitment) for the characters themselves and their social situation and how they inhabit Leonida. Shoes, sneakers, and colorways that we know carry cultural weight as items – likewise watches, sunglasses, or hats.”
items.title_en: GTA 6: All the Major New Details Revealed Today, Including Animal Species, Side Activities, and Fast Travel

items.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Simulates Tropical Storms and Hurricanes
items.excerpt: It sounds like Grand Theft Auto 6 will take open world weather effects to another level, with simulated tropical storms and hurricanes.
items.content_text: It sounds like Grand Theft Auto 6 will take open world weather effects to another level, with simulated tropical storms and hurricanes. We already knew that GTA 6 would have an advanced weather system of some kind. But in Game Informer's GTA 6 cover story , senior associate editor Marcus Stewart described the need for Leonida to have diverse weather, due to Florida's tendency to have wild shifts in its climate. And, it seems like Rockstar has that covered. Rockstar vice president of art for lighting and rendering, Owen Shepherd, told Stewart, "We have re-engineered our weather system to make everything much more localized and persistent," and that "the world features new fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map." We already know that GTA 6 is going to have a map that's three times larger than the ones found in Grand Theft Auto 5 and in Red Dead Redemption 2 , so it's even more impressive that the game will be able to simulate moving storm systems. In practice, this will absolutely mean you can get localized rain showers in one area, while the next area is sunny. But while that alone wouldn't necessarily be groundbreaking, it seems like weather systems will have lasting effects on the environment. According to Stewart, he was told that "GTA 6's rain creates realistic rainbows under the right lighting conditions, and that recently showered areas will remain wet on the ground and create persistent puddles once the storm passes." That'd be cool enough if the weather in Leonida only got as extreme as a thunderstorm but in real life, Florida is known to have more unpredictable weather. Luckily, GTA 6 will also have simulated tropical storms and hurricanes, which will wreak havoc on the environment. Shepherd says that these storms will have "heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics and a lot of rain combine so that everything is dripping wet, water is gushing off roof edges and lampposts, thunder rumbles and flashes of lighting light up the clouds dramatically." Unfortunately, Game Informer's cover story doesn't come with video that shows these weather systems in action, but combined with the persistent effects weather can have on the environment, my imagination is running wild. Will there be flooding in the streets? Will buildings and trees get knocked down? There are a ton of possibilities, and I already want to jump in and go storm chasing. GTA 6 launches on November 19, so we won't have to wait too long to see what the weather can do.

items.title: The Steam Frame: VR’s Future or the Beginning of the End?
items.content_text: I’ve always loved VR. I bought my current headset – a Pico 4 – three years ago, for around £300/$400. While that particular model isn’t available in America for very questionable reasons , if I wanted an alternative and was willing to enter Zuckerberg’s walled garden (I am not), a Quest 3S is even cheaper. With good wireless support, color pass-through cameras and a robust native library of games even before connecting to a PC, I felt VR had finally arrived at where it should be. A new world of games, accessible for less than a Nintendo Switch 2. While I understand RAM prices are skyrocketing, when Valve announced its entry into the lightweight, wireless VR field would cost a wallet-obliterating £889/$1,059 for the cheapest Steam Frame model , my heart sank. And worse yet, it wasn’t launching any new software to accompany it. The Steam Frame’s killer app? A native port of Half-Life: Alyx, an admittedly excellent game, but one released in 2020 with a mod scene that has largely moved on due to lack of support from Valve itself. Even the store page for the Steam Frame proudly displays Moss Book 2 as one of the great games you could play on the Frame. And while it is great (as are many VR games – there’s a library here dwarfing any console for sure), the developers, Polyarc, recently closed its doors due to a lack of sales and funding, even after releasing a non-VR version. While there’s still a steady trickle of VR games, on the PC side of things, almost all the big players have tapped out. There are no big AAA releases to look forward to. No big next step for VR design. And the buy-in price to access this via Valve’s new hardware is triple what I’d be willing to pay for a headset. Quadruple that, in the case of Meta’s newly-announced lightweight VR glasses . Despite all this, I love VR. It has filled the hole in my life where lightgun games and oddball titles with one-off peripherals (pour one out for Samba De Amigo and Steel Battalion) used to live. It features some of the coolest mech games , most terrifying trips through haunted wastelands and experimental arcade experiences around. VR isn’t going anywhere, with a slow but steady flow of new hardware and modders continually patching VR support into older classic games . But I also cannot fathom what the future of VR looks like, or if it even has one at all. VR has filled the hole in my life where lightgun games and oddball titles with one-off peripherals used to live If Valve and Meta are to be believed, VR isn’t an alternative to a lower-end handheld console. It is the domain of enthusiast tech nerds with money to burn. It is a whole medium with almost no major studios involved anymore, and even Meta’s big announcement showcase last week featured little more than rehashes and ports of ‘classic’ games, and many of those will remain exclusive to Meta hardware too. Valve has all the money in the world but without investing some of it into developers, I worry that unless the Frame sells unexpectedly well, that it too will lose interest in this field. While I love my cheap, versatile little headset, and adore adding VR mods to classic games to experience them in new ways , I’d like for VR to grow and be supported once more. To be able to point to something big and new and exciting on the horizon to get other people on board with me. And a port of a six-year-old game, however good it was, isn’t going to cut it. Hookshot is also partnered with the tech experts at Digital Foundry and is partnered commercially with IGN. As Hookshot’s dedicated PC gaming site, it’s got news of the latest releases , updates and mod drops , plus weekly roundups and a must-play monthly playlist to help you keep up with the never-ending deluge of new experiences.

items.title: Why Control Resonant Developer Remedy Avoided Using Yellow Paint to Guide Players
items.excerpt: Control Resonant's director has explained how the team chose to handle exploration in a way that doesn't feel like it is holding the player's hand with things like yellow paint.
items.content_text: Control Resonant's director has explained how the team chose to handle exploration in a way that doesn't feel like it is holding the player's hand with things like yellow paint. For a number of years now, some gamers have begun to feel like games provide players with more guidance than is necessary. One example of this is yellow paint, which basically highlights exactly where the player needs to go during exploration. Critics say that when this sort of navigation aid is heavy handed, it can be distracting and remove a sense of agency. Marvel's Wolverine, for example, was heavily criticized for its "fart gas," a blue mist that Wolverine can sniff out to find his objective. Soon after launch, developer Insomniac added the ability to toggle it off . Control Resonant developer Remedy doesn't beat players over the head. It is an open-world game with zones that the player can freely explore, though sometimes it isn't always crystal clear where to go. Control Resonant director Mikael Kasurinen explained on the Dropped Frames podcast (via Kotaku ) that it was important for the player to feel like they were figuring out this convoluted world themselves, rather than following flashing arrows. He noted that for players to get the most out of the world, they had to be active participants. “It’s so important that the players feel like they’re the ones figuring it out,” said Kasurinen. “It’s the job of us as creators to… I mean, it is a crafted experience at the end of the day, right? You have to find the right balance between ‘here’s the world’ and ‘here are the different themes and elements that you have to pay attention to.’ But it has to feel like it’s on you to make a decision on what to do with those elements that you see within the world. If it feels like it’s like ‘go here,’ it’s not anymore a decision for the player. Somebody already decided for you.” The director went on to note that Remedy recognized that it risked alienating players looking for a more guided and simple experience, but for those that really engage with it, it will be more rewarding and interesting. “People will be coming back to this game, exploring, trying to kind of find out things and so on," he added. "It’s not something that you kind of go through, you did what you were told, and you’re done. It feels like, no, I made some choices in this game and you have that little little question: Did I make the right choices? And I want that f***ing question. I want people to think like that. I want them to kind of, you know, doubt, go back, check again, see what they could do differently, because that’s life. That’s what makes it sticky and interesting.” Another developer with a similar philosophy to Remedy's is Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons studio Invoke. Dominic Guay, General Manager at Invoke Studios, told IGN at gamescom 2026 that the developers avoided putting waypoints into the game because they want players to actually explore . The open-world single-player action-adventure goes easy on the hand-holding by ditching traditional quest markers that guide players directly from one story section to the next. While it does have a compass on the top of the screen — which you can turn off — the player is left to work out where to go by exploring, talking to NPCs, and thinking about what to do next. “We wanted them to engage with the world, to figure things out and feel that when they found things, it was based on their actions and not just blindly trusting a waypoint,” Guay said. IGN's Control Resonant review returned an 8/10. We said: "Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse," reads an excerpt from the review. "While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue."

items.title: The Witcher 3 Fans Relieved to Find Low-Polygon Pigeons Have Survived the Remaster Process
items.excerpt: The Witcher 3 Remastered brings tons of graphics improvements, but developer CD Projekt Red has left one incredibly important creature as it was: the pigeon.
items.content_text: The Witcher 3 Remastered brings tons of graphics improvements, but developer CD Projekt Red has left one incredibly important creature as it was: the pigeon. Ahead of the remaster's public release, updated pigeon models were found in the game, but it only seems to apply to pigeons that are hanging out on the ground. Still, some people were upset with the assumed change, with one person posting the new ground-based model with the old flying one in a Reddit post captioned, "Gone, but never forgotten." Pigeons Remastered by u/abdx80 in Witcher3 Luckily, it seems like the beloved low-poly pigeon has survived the remaster, as it was spotted by Kotaku Editor-in-Chief Ethan Gach on X / Twitter out in the wild. Apparently, The Witcher 3 uses different pigeon models for flying and grounded birds! If anything, the low-polygon pigeon looks even funnier in the remaster, as it shows the (lack of) detail even better with the updated lighting. This is a false alarm.
